acquisition_methods.acquisition_details: Protein-protein interactions mapped by affinity purification-mass spectrometry (AP-MS) on endogenously tagged cell lines. Seventeen genes were endogenously tagged in MDA-MB-468 and AP-MS data acquired under three conditions (untreated, paclitaxel treated, vorinostat treated), with 34 additional genes in the tagging process at the time of the preprint.

Proteome-wide complex and interaction mapping by size-exclusion chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry (SEC-MS), used as an orthogonal mass spectrometry-based approach to AP-MS. SEC-MS on MDA-MB-468 cells under three conditions identified 72 of 100 chromatin modifiers, 52 of them integral components of protein complexes, and detected PPI profiles of over a thousand complexes. SEC-MS in KOLF2 iPSCs and derivatives uncovered more than 700 protein complexes in both parental iPSCs and differentiated neurons.

Spatial subcellular organization mapped by immunofluorescence staining and high-resolution confocal microscopy using the Human Protein Atlas resource of antibodies, with automated fixation and permeabilization protocols established on a pipetting robot for the MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 cell lines.

Genetic perturbation mapping by single-cell CRISPR screens. A CRISPR lentiviral library targeting 100 chromatin factors with 6 guide RNAs per gene was designed; MDA-MB-468 and KOLF2 CRISPR lines expressing inducible dCas9 were generated and characterized; single-cell CRISPR screens were performed using the 10x Genomics 3'HT kit.

d4d_fields.description: The June 2026 Data Release of Cell Maps for Artificial Intelligence (CM4AI), the Functional Genomics Grand Challenge in the NIH Bridge2AI program. CM4AI generates multi-modal data including protein-protein interaction (PPI), spatial localization, and genetic perturbation data in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells (with and without paclitaxel or vorinostat treatment) and KOLF2.1J induced pluripotent stem cells (with and without differentiation). This Beta release includes: Perturb-seq data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment and undifferentiated (parental) KOLF2.1J iPSCs; SEC-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment, undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs, and iPSC-derived neuron progenitor cells (NPCs), neurons, and cardiomyocytes; AP-MS data for MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with treatment; and immunofluorescence (IF) images in MDA-MB-468 breast cancer cells with and without treatment. CM4AI's overarching mission is to produce ethical, AI-ready datasets of cell architecture, inferred from multimodal data collected for human cell lines, to enable transformative biomedical AI research. CM4AI output data are packaged with provenance graphs and rich metadata as AI-ready datasets in RO-Crate format using the FAIRSCAPE framework. CM4AI is a collaboration of UCSD, UCSF, Stanford, UVA, Yale, UT Austin, UA Birmingham, Simon Fraser University, and the Hastings Center.
